seo.description: Plan El Jadida: UNESCO Portuguese City, Cistern, Bastion of the Angel, fishing port with blue boats, Medina, Mellah, El Jadida beach and Sidi Bouzid on Morocco’s Atlantic Doukkala coast.

name: El Jadida
hero_subtitle: Atlantic trade winds, UNESCO Portuguese ramparts, a glowing underground cistern and a working harbour of blue fishing boats — the Doukkala coast at its most characterful.

overview.title: Welcome to El Jadida — Portuguese stone on the Atlantic
overview.p1: El Jadida sits on Morocco’s Atlantic Doukkala coast, about an hour south of Casablanca. Its heart is the UNESCO-listed Portuguese City (Mazagan): thick ramparts, the Bastion of the Angel, and the famous underground cistern where a shaft of light falls on still water.
overview.p2: Beyond the walls: a working fishing port packed with blue boats, the old Jewish Mellah, Medina lanes and souks, the city beach, and the resort strip of Sidi Bouzid with its open Atlantic horizon. This is rocky and sandy Atlantic shore — not desert, not lagoon kite camps, not mountain trail country.
overview.p3: Two to three days cover the Portuguese core, the port and one beach or coastal outing. Spring and autumn bring milder air; summer is for swimming when the Atlantic allows.

plage.title: El Jadida Beach

port.title: Fishing Port

sidi_bouzid.title: Sidi Bouzid

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day plan for El Jadida
itinerary.subtitle: Portuguese core first, then harbour and Atlantic beach time.

day1.title: Portuguese City
day1.desc: Cistern, ramparts, Bastion of the Angel and medina lanes.

day2.title: Port & Mellah
day2.desc: Fishing harbour, Mellah and souks; evening on the walls.

day3.title: Atlantic beach
day3.desc: Sidi Bouzid or city beach; optional Haouzia coast.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Enter the Portuguese Cistern early for quieter light on the water.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Walk the walls to the Bastion of the Angel and Atlantic viewpoints.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Souks and a simple dinner inside or near the old town.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Blue boats, nets and the working harbour atmosphere.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Old Jewish quarter and surrounding medina streets.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Sunset light on the ramparts if wind and access allow.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Resort beach south of town for sand and open ocean.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Closer sand or a coastal stretch toward Haouzia.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Port-side grilled fish before the train or road north.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: Trains and buses link Casablanca (CMN). Petits taxis cover town, Sidi Bouzid and the station; agree prices for longer coastal hops.

bargain.title: Wind & sun
bargain.desc: Atlantic trade winds can be strong. Bring a layer for the ramparts and high SPF for beach days.

water.title: Tickets & cash
water.desc: The cistern has a small entry fee. Carry dirhams for taxis, port snacks and medina shops.

q1.question: How many days in El Jadida?
q1.answer: Two days cover the Portuguese City, cistern, ramparts and port. Three days add Sidi Bouzid beach time or a short trip to Azemmour.

q2.question: Is El Jadida only about the Portuguese ruins?
q2.answer: The UNESCO walls and cistern are the headline, but the fishing port, Mellah, souks and Atlantic beaches give a full coastal-town stay.

q3.question: How do I get to El Jadida?
q3.answer: Fly into Casablanca (CMN), then continue by train or road in about an hour. Direct coaches also run from major cities.

q4.question: Best time to visit?
q4.answer: April–June and September–November for milder weather and fewer crowds. Summer is for swimming; winter can be windy and wetter.
